Hi Jonas / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our legal team's annotated DPA (tracked changes) — primary asks: tighter cross-border transfer language, an expanded subprocessors list, and clarified breach notification timelines. We also flagged the standard escrow / audit language.

High-level items we want to resolve in round 1:
- EU data transfer mechanism: can Redwood adopt the EU Standard Terms + our requested addendum?
- Operator subprocessor obligations: we need direct liability and audit rights for key subprocessors (logging + telemetry).
- Retention: customer-controlled retention for certain PII fields.

Patrick O'Connell (cc) is our procurement lead and will coordinate execution. For eSign we prefer DocuSign; please advise routing and any required internal approvals.

Attachments: Hyperscale_DPA_Redlines_v1.pdf

Cheers,

Subject: Re: Fwd: Hyperscale DPA redlines (round 1)

Jonas — reviewed Hyperscale's PDF. Summary of counsel-first positions and suggested responses below. I circled in the attached synthesis where our standard positions differ.

1) EU transfers: we do not sign third-party addenda that alter controller-processor mechanics. Proposed compromise: Accept EU SCCs (latest version) plus a limited EU-US addendum that mirrors our existing transfer exhibit; we will not accept customer language that imposes reverse obligations on our subprocessors beyond what SCCs require.

2) Subprocessors / audit rights: We can list key infrastructure subprocessors and offer a covenant to notify customers 30 days before adding a new operator. We can't give unlimited audit rights to customers for hosted infra providers; instead propose: (a) material-subprocessor evidence (SOC2 Type II reports) on request under NDA, and (b) an annual compliance attestation for platforms that process Hyperscale production data.

3) Breach notification and retention: We can meet 72-hour notification for incidents impacting customer data (consistent with our incident playbook). For retention, we can include contract terms allowing for customer-initiated retention configuration for certain data classes — will need product sign-off on the implementation window (30–60 days).

4) Liability / indemnities: We can accept a limited carve for processor-level breaches tied to our negligence, but we will not accept unlimited consequential liability. Suggest a commercial escalation to Sales if customer insists.

Evidentiary attachments to send: current SOC2 report (redacted), subprocessors inventory sheet, and our incident response summary.

DocuSign routing: I'll take primary owner for the legal milestone. Kimberly / Jonas: if commercial signoff on the compromise above, I can prepare a negotiated version for eSign and route via DocuSign and include an internal approver chain (legal -> sales manager -> finance).

Next steps I recommend: 
- Jonas: confirm Hyperscale is ok with SCCs + our transfer exhibit (I can draft language).
- Kimberly: confirm we can offer the retention configuration timeline (product/engineering check).
- Mateo: prep SOC2 + subprocessor inventory for redaction and attachment.

Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com

Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hyperscale DPA redlines (round 1) — summary and proposed path

Claire / Hyperscale team — appreciate the detailed redlines. Quick summary of our proposed path so we can align:

- Transfers: Redwood will execute the EU SCCs (latest) + our standard transfer exhibit. Monica will circulate suggested exhibit language by EOD today.
- Subprocessors: We will provide a current inventory and SOC2 evidence. For audit, we propose the evidence + annual attestation approach rather than customer inspections.
- Breach / retention: 72-hour notification; retention configuration available within 45 days of contract execution for implicated data classes.
- Liability: standard processor limits; open to commercial discussion if you require broader language.

DocuSign: once legal confirms the negotiated redline, Monica will prepare the v1 for DocuSign. My preferred routing: Monica (owner) -> Kimberly (sales manager approval) -> Finance (exec approval) -> Hyperscale signatory. Monica, please advise if legal needs an internal escalation step.

Attached: redlines_synthesis.docx (internal summary).

Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hyperscale DPA redlines (round 1) — summary and proposed path

Thanks Kimberly / Monica — this is helpful and faster than expected. A few clarifying Qs before we proceed to negotiated redline: 

1) SCCs + transfer exhibit: Hyperscale legal will accept SCCs plus your transfer exhibit if the exhibit is materially equivalent to the protections in the SCCs. Please mark in-track the exact lines you plan to change so we can do a quick legal compare.

2) Subprocessor evidence cadence: we prefer a 30-day prior notice for new subprocessors for any that will process production PII, and a commitment to provide SOC2 for any such new subprocessor within 10 business days of request. Is that feasible?

3) DocuSign: we can accept the routing you proposed. Patrick will be our signatory for execution. Please route the DocuSign envelope to legal@hyperscale.io and cc: patrick.oconnell@hyperscale.io so procurement can track.

If you can send the negotiated v1 by tomorrow EOD we can review and aim to complete execution next week.

Claire
Claire Dupont
Head of Legal Operations
Hyperscale Inc.
